HAIR UP: ALL of her glossy pure BLACK hair (never brown) is swept UP and gathered into the tall high chignon on top of her head under the crown, smooth at the nape; NO hair hanging loose down her back or over her shoulders. SLEEVES: very long, very wide, flowing sleeves that fall well past her hands and hang PAST her ankles all the way down until they TOUCH THE FLOOR, ONE single sleeve layer (no shorter outer sleeve on top); the brocade flows and drapes softly like heavy silk, never stiff. FABRIC: thick gold-embroidered brocade with a graceful, flowing drape. COLOUR RULE: all colours fresh, clear and luminous, never dusty or greyed; the royal golden yellow is the DOMINANT colour of the robe, mantle, sleeves and skirt (more than half of everything visible), black silk richly embroidered with gold thread (the yellow clearly more than the black) is the second colour (collar, inner robe, wide borders and a few panels); the yellow is rich warm royal golden yellow, a honey-gold close to hex #EFBD69 (medium depth, 18K gold tone), not pale cream, not beige/tan/ochre, not heavy mustard, not lemon; the crown, hairpin and jewellery gold in the same 18K tone; gold only as thin accents on the borders; NOT an all-yellow robe. All flowers, birds and the dragon are fine silk-thread embroidery stitched directly into the fabric, flat and integrated with the cloth, following its folds, not appliqué, not pasted patches, not raised. The silk has real weight: the wide sleeves and robe hang and fold naturally under their own weight, with natural creases, never stiff, flat or board-like. Pose: calm standing pose; she holds a round fan of deep crimson silk embroidered with gold dragons, handle of gold carved with dragons, with crimson-and-gold dragon tassels in a contrasting colour, not the robe colour, the item held below the chin, the hand really gripping it, the whole face fully visible. Her hands and body: the round fan held up in one hand at chest height, gently turned to show its painting, the other hand lightly touching its tassel. Every hairpin is inserted into the hair pointing upward or backward with dangles hanging down, no hairpin horizontal or sticking out to the side.
